claims.claim: The Epistle to Diognetus is an anonymous Christian apologetic letter whose author calls himself a “student of the Apostles” and otherwise remains unknown.

It is addressed to a man named Diognetus, described as “most excellent” and likely a high‑ranking pagan official who asked detailed questions about Christian worship, the Christian contempt of death, and the rejection of Greek and Jewish religions.
The purpose of the work is to answer Diognetus’s inquiries and to defend Christianity by contrasting Christian practice with pagan idol worship and Jewish superstition.

That manuscript was first printed in 1592 under the name of Justin Martyr, and the original codex was destroyed in the fire that engulfed Strasbourg during the Franco‑Prussian War in 1870, leaving only later transcriptions.

Because of its early date and articulate presentation of Christian doctrine and moral teaching, the epistle is often grouped with the Apostolic Fathers and is regarded as a valuable example of second‑century Christian apologetics.
